Within St. Margaret’s Court I stood alone,

Whose wasted right hand gambled ’gainst his left

If only she could reach there before this labouring anguish burst from her breast to her lips—if only she could feel the hold of Gerty’s arms while she shook in the ague-fit of fear that was coming upon her!
Sweat--was it that hot--or was he sick--the ague--fever--the rain water--crying--
Cadwallader—“when he has come out on the other side of the mud with an ague.”
“She whips it to a jelly,” the piano player was singing now, and banging on the keys with such might that an empty gin bottle on top of the piano seemed to be seized with the ague.
Heathcliff, having stared his son into an ague of confusion, uttered a scornful laugh.
